farquharson_usage: desire — the genus of motivating states encompassing appetite (ἐπιθυμία), spirit (θυμός), and wish (βούλησις); the proximate efficient cause of all animal locomotion; 'the last in the chain of things moved to move something else' (701a1).
notes: Genus covering ἐπιθυμία, θυμός, βούλησις. The claim that desire is the proximate mover is the central thesis of the treatise.

farquharson_usage: imagination — the faculty that presents objects to desire; a form of discrimination shared with sensation and thought; moves animals by arousing desire; can produce involuntary movement without rational mandate.
notes: Farquharson renders 'imagination'; contested whether this captures the perceptual-presentational sense. Nussbaum prefers 'appearance' in some contexts. MA shows phantasia operating both rationally (practical syllogism) and sub-rationally (involuntary movement).

farquharson_usage: movement, locomotion — change of place; the specific kind of change investigated in this treatise; requires both internal immovable point and external immovable ground.
notes: In MA, κίνησις refers primarily to locomotion (φορά), distinct from its broader use in Physics covering all four kinds of change.

farquharson_usage: syllogism of actions — the logical structure whereby a universal major premise about the good plus a particular minor premise yields action as conclusion; 'the conclusion I must make a coat is an action' (701a20).
notes: The practical syllogism yields action, not a proposition, as its conclusion. NE gives the ethical framing; MA gives the psychological-mechanical version.

farquharson_usage: the good — the final cause that initiates movement; the object of desire; may be actual good, apparent good, or the pleasant.
notes: Not every intelligible object moves, but only the end in the domain of conduct.

farquharson_usage: the unmoved mover — that which causes motion without being moved; in cosmology, the mover of the heavens; in animals, the object of desire as final cause.
notes: The cosmological chapters (1-5) establish the requirement; the zoological chapters (6-11) apply it to animal desire.

farquharson_usage: connate spirit — the bodily medium through which the soul transmits movement to the limbs; capable of expansion and contraction; stands to the soul as the moved joint-point stands to the unmoved.
notes: Contested whether identical with the pneuma of Generation of Animals II.3; Nussbaum argues for continuity. Ontological status unclear: instrument of soul, fifth element, or heated air?

farquharson_usage: sense-perception — faculty of discrimination that alongside phantasia and thought can present objects to desire and supply the minor premise of the practical syllogism.
notes: In MA, sensation functions primarily as one of three faculties (alongside phantasia and thought) that supply the particular premise.

farquharson_usage: alteration — bodily change (heating/chilling) that mediates between psychological states and locomotion; imaginations produce the same bodily effects as real objects.
notes: The psychosomatic dimension: phantasia causes ἀλλοίωσις (heating/chilling), which causes locomotion.

farquharson_usage: purpose — belongs 'both to intellect and to desire' (700b22-23); a hybrid faculty combining thought and desire.
notes: Farquharson: 'purpose'; often translated 'deliberate choice' following NE III.2-3.
